utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Hadije Fazliu this is the in-court summary. The witness describes the events of March 1999 in the Srbica municipality, when many villages were attacked by Serb forces. She states that on 26th March, 1999, Serb forces shelled her village Turicevac from the direction of Broje village. The villagers were forced to flee. The witness describes the plight of the refugees as they travelled through different municipalities to the Albanian border. She describes the forces involved in the deportation. End of in-court summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'll move on to the next witness. This is Hamide Fondaj. I'd like to tender 05044 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00626, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00627.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now read the in-court summary for Hamide Fondaj. The witness is a Muslim woman from the village of Pecane in the Suva Reka municipality. She describes the forcible expulsions of Kosovo Albanians from Pecane in March 1999. On the 21st of March, 1999, her village and others in the area came under the attack of Serb forces. Together with other displaced persons, she ended up in the village of Belanica through a route that was not blocked by the Serbs. On the 1st of April, 1999, Serb police, military, and paramilitary attacked Belanica and expelled the occupants. Ms. Fondaj witnessed this attack. She and her family had to spend the night on a tractor-trailer and the next night they started to leave Belanica. They were stopped many times by the police who threatened them and demanded money. En route to the border, she witnessed many Albanian civilians detained behind barbed wire in Malisevo. The convoy was subjected to abuse by the Serbs. Outside Ostrozub they had to run over a lot of "plis" this is the Albanian hats that were taken from the men and thrown on the ground. Houses were being set on fire within that village. On the 4th of April, the witness crossed the border to Albania via Vrmnica. That's the end of this in-court summary. I'll now move on to witness Ali Hoti. I'd like to tender into evidence 05010.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00628, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00629.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I will now read his in-court summary. The witness describes the attack by Serb forces on Velika Krusa, Orahovac municipality, on the 25th of March, 1999. He describes the forces that carried out the attack. He saw these forces set his own house on fire as well as those in surrounding villages. He also saw police and soldiers looting property in his village. As a consequence of the attack on Velika Krusa, the population was forced to flee to the hills around the village. The witness and his family joined a group of villagers and headed to Nogavac where numerous other refugees had gathered. While in Nogavac, the witness, who is a doctor, treated several survivors of the Batusha barn massacre, including Mehmet Krasniqi. On the 2nd of April, 1999, the witness joined a large convoy of Kosovo Albanians heading for Albania. At the Albanian border, Serb police confiscated all IDs and documents. End of in-court summary. In the final witness is Krasniqi, Florim Elmi. I'd like to tender 05081.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00630, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00631, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'll now read the in-court summary of Florim Krasniqi. The witness is from the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will wait for my colleague to complete the reading of the summary and then I will -- Albanian on English channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: The witness is from the village of Mirosavlje in the municipality of Urosevac. On the 4th of April, 1999, the witness saw military vehicles on the red from Gnjilane to Urosevac shelling the villages of Rakovica and Zlatare. The following day the witness heard shelling, firing, and tanks moving in the direction of Pojatiste. As a consequence, about 1.000 displaced persons from surrounding villages arrived in his village. On the 7th of April, 1999, the witness saw burning houses in Sojevo and Kamena Glava also in the municipality of Urosevac. The following day a tank and several military APCs came to the witness's village. Together with others he headed to the centre of Urosevac. En route they encountered several military check-points where people in the convoy were harassed and insulted. At the outskirts of Urosevac, the witness was stopped at a police check-point. On 14th April, 1999, the witness left Urosevac. He got on a bus and went to the border town of Djeneral Jankovic. At the border police demanded identification papers. The witness was ordered to collect the papers, which he did, and they were then returned. The bus continued to the train station, where the police separated the people and collected money from the heads of the families. The witness states that they were eventually ordered to walk to Macedonia along the railway tracks. End of Florim Krasniqi's in-court summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, Your Honour. I would just like to say that having worked diligently on preparing the case I noted that some of the statements of those witnesses have not been tendered into the evidence. And since I noticed some discrepancies, I would like to ask permission to do it myself if it is judged to be in the interests of justice and the determination of the truth. That's all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How many of these additional statements do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I was not aware that the Prosecution would do that now, I don't have this information here; but I could obtain it, I could look for it, and then inform the Trial Chamber if it is necessary. That's all I had to say. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. I take it from what you are saying you are not proposing to tender those things today, but we'll perhaps do it after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely what I had in mind, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If there are other statements of these four witnesses who have been dealt with today, which statements, in your view, are materially different from the statements that have been tendered? You can anticipate that the Chamber would be prepared to receive them. We don't want to have additional statements just because they exist; but if there is a material difference, we certainly would appreciate that that could be relevant to your case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour. I said this out of an abundance of caution. I don't want to burden the Trial Chamber with things that are immaterial. So only if there are any discrepancies that are really very important.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can I note --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- I don't like to interfere. May I just note, Your Honours, that this is a matter that we already have a ruling on. And I don't think there are any statements, so I don't think much will come out of this. But it ought to have been a matter that was addressed in the response to the -- to the filings so the Court would have had that -- the benefit of that when the Court made its decision earlier on. That is all I wish to say, but I'm sure counsel will review it and do what is appropriate. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, that issue will be considered, if it is, after the break that Mr. Djordjevic is impressed with the need to offer some further statement or statements, those matters will be considered.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In accordance with the programme that we have indicated, the Chamber will now adjourn to -- for just over a week, which will allow the observance of both the Western and the Eastern Easter vacations relevant to various counsel and to the accused; that will mean that we continue our evidence commencing on Tuesday, the 21st of April, when we will commence at 11.00 a.m. and continue sitting until 4.45. The Chamber would hope that this break, which is the first that we've had after some ten weeks of sitting, will enable counsel, both for the Prosecution and the accused, to review their preparation and plan ahead for what is to continue in the trial. The Chamber would also hope that the opportunity will enable counsel to refresh themselves and to spend a little time with their families. So with those thoughts, we wish you well for the Easter and resume now on Tuesday, the 21st of April.
